stem.text: Read lines 8 and 9. What does 'bolted out of the house' mean here?

options.execution: To bolt food is a real second sense of the verb, and the passage gives him no food to bolt.

options.value: Slid a bolt across to lock the door.
options.execution: The door-fastening is the sense a child meets first, and 'bolted out of the house' puts a house and a door in the same clause to support it.

options.value: Climbed out slowly using a ladder.
options.execution: The ladders and steps are line 2, inside the house and before he leaves — true, and from a different part.

options.value: Rushed out all of a sudden.

options.execution: 'Hang spring-cleaning!' is on line 8 itself. True, in the window, and it is what he said rather than how he left.

stem.text: Look at lines 9 to 12. What does Fraulein Rottenmeier find in the wardrobe?

options.value: An expression of horror on her face.

options.value: An old straw hat left out on the table.
options.execution: True at line 15, three lines past the end of this window, where Tinette is told to take it away.

options.value: Clothes that had grown too small for the child.
options.execution: She went up to see what to keep and what to throw away, which invites this.

options.value: A heap of rolls at the bottom of it.
